newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER WOODS DECLINES CLINTON INVITE TO ATTEND GAME.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER WOODS DECLINES CLINTON INVITE TO ATTEND GAME.

text.p: President Clinton invited Masters golf winner Tiger Woods to join him at Shea Stadium to mark the 50th anniversary of Jackie Robinson breaking baseball's colour line, but Woods politely declined, the White House said Tuesday.
A White House spokesman, Barry Toiv, said the White House extended the invitation on Clinton's behalf to Woods on Monday, a day after the 21-year-old golfing phenomenon won the Masters by 12 strokes.
"He (Woods) felt very strongly that he needed some time out of the limelight, and tonight would very much have been in the limelight, obviously," Toiv said.
Clinton Tuesday night was leading an observance at Shea Stadium of Robinson's status as the first black to play in the major leagues 50 years ago.
Toiv said the president did not feel Woods was snubbing him.
"Not at all," he said. "Everyone here understood perfectly. They very politely declined. Clearly, somewhere, at some point, they will get together."
Clinton, an avid golfer, watched Woods' triumph on television. Clinton is recovering from surgery to repair a knee tendon he tore March 14 at the Florida estate of pro golfer Greg Norman.
